contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Loading indicators use animation to grab attention, mitigate perceived latency, and indicate that an activity is in progress.

They should be used when progress isn’t detectable, or when it’s not necessary to indicate how long an activity will take.

While similar in function to circular progress indicators, loading indicators are a better alternative for short processes between 200ms and 5s.

contentChunks.footer: Use a loading indicator when a background process is running
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator in loading state with “Getting your device ready...”.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Choose a loading or progress indicator that corresponds to the expected wait time and type of process. 

If the wait is very long, consider allowing users to navigate away from the page while the process finishes up.

Expected wait time
Recommendation
Instant (under 200ms)No indicator
Short (between 200ms and 5s)Loading indicator
Long (Over 5s)Progress indicator

contentChunks.footer: Instant (under 200ms): Display the content immediately
contentChunks.altText: Content appearing on a screen quickly without a loading indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Short (between 200ms and 5s): Use a loading indicator
contentChunks.altText: Content appearing on a screen with a slight lag and a loading indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Long (over 5s): Use a progress indicator
contentChunks.altText: Content appearing on a screen with a long lag and a progress indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
When a process can transition from indeterminate (unknown progress) to determinate (known remaining progress), transition between the corresponding progress indicators. 

Don’t transition a loading indicator into a progress indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Transition from an indeterminate progress indicator to a determinate progress indicator
contentChunks.altText: A screen transitioning from an indeterminate progress indicator to a determinate progress indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid transitioning from a loading indicator to a determinate progress indicator
contentChunks.altText: A screen transitioning from a loading indicator to a determinate progress indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Active indicator

The active indicator is a looping shape morph sequence composed of seven unique Material 3 shapes.

More about the Material shape library

contentChunks.footer: The active indicator morphs shape to capture attention
contentChunks.altText: Active indicator with shape morph.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Container (optional)

When the container is visible, the active indicator should change color from primary to on-primary-container.

The container should be visible when the loading indicator is placed over other content. This helps it stand out better by giving it a stronger contrast. It’s not needed when the loading indicator is placed directly on a surface.

The container should be used with pull-to-refresh behavior.

contentChunks.footer: The container is a circle that provides extra contrast from body content
contentChunks.altText: Active indicator with container.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Placement
While loading a page or container, the loading indicator should be centered on the element.

contentChunks.footer: Center the loading indicator in the middle of the page or container
contentChunks.altText: Active indicator with shape morph centered on a screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: When loading more items on a page with existing content, place the loading indicator in the empty space where the new content will appear. Avoid overlapping existing content.

contentChunks.footer: Center the loading indicator in the empty space where content will appear
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator with shape morph underneath photos in a photo app.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Loading indicators can be placed within other components, such as buttons, to indicate that the action is ongoing, such as validating a form or checking for updates.

contentChunks.footer: Loading indicators can be placed in buttons that take a few seconds to take effect
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator in a button.

contentChunks.footer: Use loading indicators to show progress without taking up much space
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator as the icon in a tab.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Responsive layout

Loading indicators default to 48dp, but the size is flexible. It should be between 24dp to 240dp, depending on the placement and the breakpoint. Avoid exceeding the minimum and maximum sizes.

The ratio between the container and the active indicator stays the same when resizing the loading indicator. 

Reserve very large progress indicators for large and extra-large windows, like desktop.

contentChunks.footer: Loading indicators can range in size from 24–240dp
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicators can range from 24dps to 240dps.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Larger windows

As the pane or window size grows, consider scaling the loading indicator as well, so it remains proportional in size to the empty space around it. The loading indicator shouldn’t exceed 240dp.

contentChunks.footer: The loading indicator’s default size is ideal for mobile and other compact windows. The loading indicator should scale up in larger windows.
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator on mobile and tablet screens.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behavior

Pull-to-refresh

The loading indicator is used in pull-to-refresh on Jetpack Compose only.

Pull-to-refresh is an Android system feature that manually refreshes screen content with an action or gesture. It’s used at the beginning of lists, grid lists, and card collections where the most recent content appears.

It’s best to use pull-to-refresh with dynamic content that can have frequent updates, where people have a high chance of seeing new content after refreshing.

contentChunks.footer: The loading indicator for pull-to-refresh can appear on top of the content or adjacent to it
contentChunks.altText: A loading indicator can appear above content in pull-to-refresh.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Threshold requirements

To ensure intentional usage of the pull-to-refresh gesture, the loading indicator must pass a threshold before the app will refresh.

contentChunks.footer: After passing the threshold, completing the gesture initiates a refresh
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator with screen refresh after threshold time has passed.

contentChunks.footer: Reversing the gesture past the threshold will cancel the refresh action
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator reversed can cancel refresh action.

contentChunks.htmlValue: The loading indicator remains visible until the refresh activity completes and any new content is visible, or someone navigates away from the refreshing content.

contentChunks.footer: Keep the loading indicator in view until the activity is completed to provide status of the refresh activity
contentChunks.altText: A loading indicator at the top of a screen, which appears until content loads.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t scroll the loading indicator off-screen, as it hides the status of the refresh activity. It could imply that the refresh activity is associated with a specific component, such as a card, instead of the entire screen.
contentChunks.altText: A loading indicator that scrolls off screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to do the following with assistive technology:

  • Navigate to the loading indicator
  • Understand what progress the indicator is communicating
  • Initiate a content refresh without relying on a gesture
Interaction & style

The active indicator, which displays progress, provides visual contrast of at least 3:1 against most container and surface colors.

The indicator itself must have 3:1 contrast with the background, but the container does not.

contentChunks.footer: The loading indicator provides visual contrast of at least 3:1 against most background colors
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator with 3:1 color contrast.

contentChunks.htmlValue: When integrated into another component, such as a button, make sure that the active indicator provides a visual contrast of at least 3:1 against the other component.

contentChunks.footer: Ensure at least 3:1 contrast between the indicator and the surface it's on
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator with correct color contrast.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid using when the contrast is under 3:1
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator with incorrect color contrast.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Pull-to-refresh interactions can’t be accessible by just swiping. Provide an alternate way to refresh the content with a single pointer, such as placing a refresh button in a menu or directly alongside the content.

contentChunks.footer: The refresh action can be in an app bar
contentChunks.altText: Refreshing content initiated by an app bar action.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Labeling elements

Since the loading indicator is a visual cue, it needs an accessibility label to assist people who can't rely on visuals.

It should use the progress bar accessibility role. Write a label describing the purpose of the loading indicator, such as loading news article or refreshing page.

contentChunks.footer: Loading indicator labels should explain which items are loading
contentChunks.altText: Loading indicator accessibility label and role.
